content.title: Boston Marathon route: What to know about the course and where to watch
content.text: April 20, 2026, 7:26 a.m. ETThe Boston Marathon is not known as a flat and fast marathon; after all, it's known for the brutal Heartbreak Hill.But it’s also a net-downhill course, meaning if you play your cards right, it's easier than some others to set a personal record.The 2026 marathon is set to host over 30,000 competitors from almost 130 countries, with entrants from all 50 states in the country predicted to participate, the Boston Athletic Association said. There are sure to be a lot of competitors setting their own personal records at the race as well.From Main Street to Copley Square, here’s what you need to know about the Boston Marathon course.What is the Boston Marathon route? See mapThe Boston Marathon starts on Main Street in Hopkinton. Runners will then follow Route 135 through Ashland, Framingham, Natick and Wellesley to where Route 135 turns into Route 16.The course goes along Route 16 until the fire station at Commonwealth Avenue, where runners will take a right and begin the stretch of Newton Hills. After Heartbreak Hill from mile 20 to 21, runners will pass the Chestnut Hill Reservoir before turning left on to Beacon Street.At this point, runners will have just about four miles to go. They will continue through Brookline, Kenmore Square, and under Massachusetts Avenue.Finally, the famous turns come at the end: right onto Hereford Street and left onto Boylston Street for the final sprint.The Marathon ends near the Boston Public Library in Copley Square.You can see a map of the course here.How to watch the Boston Marathon in personIf you are rooting for someone who is running in the marathon and want to see them pass by, you'll need to pick your viewing spot carefully.The Boston Athletic Association has a spectator's guide available online for those want to watch in person.The guide suggests that there are eight places along the marathon route you could watch from as a spectator. Those places are:Hopkinton's Main Street at the start of the marathon (0 miles to 1.90 miles)Ashland station (1.90 miles to 4.95 miles)Framingham Train Depot (4.95 miles to 7.52 miles)Natick Common on Center Street (7.52 miles to 11.72 miles)Near the Wellesley Scream Tunnel (11.72 miles to 15.93 miles)Newton Hills (15.93 miles to 21.35 miles)Beacon Street in Brookline (22.45 miles to 24.70 miles)Boylston Street in Boston. (21.35 miles to 22.45 miles or 24.70 to Finish Line)Make sure to check the spectator's guide to see what time which racers will be passing through.How many hills in the Boston Marathon are there? And where are they?The Boston Marathon is actually mostly downhill – until the Newton Hills.The Boston Marathon course starts downhill before undulating through Wellesley.The most significant hills begin in Newton. Here, there are four hills over a six-mile stretch, culminating in Heartbreak Hill.Heartbreak Hill is a half mile long at a 5% gradient. It ends around mile 21.After Heartbreak Hill, the course is generally downhill until the finish (although it might not feel like that on tired legs). What is the elevation of the Boston Marathon?The total elevation gain of the Boston Marathon is over 800 feet, according to The Running Channel. However, runners will also lose over 1,200 feet of elevation, meaning it is a net downhill course.Don’t let that lull you into a false sense of security though: downhills are even harder on your quadricep muscles, which can often cramp up during a marathon.How to track Boston Marathon runnersIs there someone you want to track as they race today? There's an app for that.The BAA Racing App is available in both the Apple and Android store, which will allow you to track runners.If apps aren't your thing, BAA website has live tracking. If you have a runner's bib number or name you can follow their race and see the results at the finish line.When is the 2026 Boston Marathon?The 130th Boston Marathon is on Monday, April 20, which is also Patriots' Day.The Boston Marathon is traditionally held on Patriots' Day, which is the third Monday in April. This year, the marathon falls on the 251st anniversary of Patriots' Day.
